Exercise 9.2 — When CPO is TRPO, and a second CPO step by hand
      
      
        Consider the CPO subproblem $\max_xg^{	op}x$ s.t. $c+b^{	op}x\le0$, $	frac12x^{	op}Hx\le\delta$ with $H\succ0$, $\delta\gt0$ and $g
e0$ (so $q=g^{	op}H^{-1}g\gt0$). (a) Derive its dual function $D(\lambda,
u)=\max_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda,
u)$ for $\lambda\gt0$, $
u\ge0$, and show that $D$ is jointly convex. (b) Show that if the TRPO step satisfies the linearised constraint, $c+r\sqrt{2\delta/q}\le0$, then $(\lambda,
u)=(\sqrt{q/(2\delta)},0)$ minimises $D$, so CPO returns the TRPO step (the claim in the theorem of Section 3). (c) Take $g=(1,\,0.4)$, $b=(0.6,\,0.8)$, $H= egin{pmatrix}2&0.5\0.5&1\end{pmatrix}$, $\delta=0.05$, $c=-0.1$, and use the exact vectors $H^{-1}g=(16/35,\,6/35)\approx(0.457,\,0.171)$, $H^{-1}b=(4/35,\,26/35)\approx(0.114,\,0.743)$. Compute $q,r,s$, decide the regime, compute $\lambda^\star,
u^\star,x^\star$, and verify strong duality numerically.
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) $\mathcal L=g^{	op}x-
u(c+b^{	op}x)-\lambda(	frac12x^{	op}Hx-\delta)$ is strictly concave in $x$ for $\lambda\gt0$; $
abla_x\mathcal L=g-
u b-\lambda Hx=0$ gives $x= rac1\lambda H^{-1}(g-
u b)$, and substituting, $D(\lambda,
u)= rac{1}{2\lambda}(g-
u b)^{	op}H^{-1}(g-
u b)-
u c+\lambda\delta= rac{q-2
u r+
u^2s}{2\lambda}-
u c+\lambda\delta$. With $w=H^{-1/2}(g-
u b)$, affine in $
u$, the first term is $\|w\|^2/(2\lambda)$, the perspective of the convex function $	frac12\|w\|^2$; perspectives are jointly convex in $(w,\lambda)$ on $\lambda\gt0$, and composing with an affine map preserves convexity. The other two terms are linear.
            (b) Let $\lambda_0=\sqrt{q/(2\delta)}\gt0$. Multiplying the hypothesis by $\lambda_0$ gives $\lambda_0c+r\le0$. First-order conditions of the convex problem $\min_{\lambda\gt0,
u\ge0}D$ at $(\lambda_0,0)$: $\partial_\lambda D=- rac{q}{2\lambda_0^2}+\delta=0$, and $\partial_
u D= rac{
u s-r}{\lambda}-c=- rac{\lambda_0c+r}{\lambda_0}\ge0$, the correct sign for a minimiser on the boundary $
u=0$. For a convex differentiable function these conditions are sufficient, so $(\lambda_0,0)$ is a global minimiser, and Step 4 of the walkthrough maps it to $x^\star=H^{-1}g/\lambda_0=\sqrt{2\delta/q}\,H^{-1}g=x_{m TRPO}$, with value $D=\sqrt{2q\delta}=g^{	op}x_{m TRPO}$.
            (c) Using the exact inverse vectors, $q=92/175\approx0.526$, $r=72/175\approx0.411$, $s=116/175\approx0.663$. $c^2/s=7/464\approx0.0151\lt2\delta=0.1$: the hyperplane cuts the trust region. The exact TRPO test is $c+r\sqrt{2\delta/q}\approx+0.079\gt0$, so (b) does not apply and $
u^\star\gt0$. Here $q-r^2/s=196/725\approx0.2703$ and $2\delta-c^2/s=197/2320\approx0.0849$, giving $\lambda_a=\sqrt{ rac{q-r^2/s}{2\delta-c^2/s}}=56/\sqrt{985}\approx1.784$. It lies inside the exact $\Lambda_a=[0,\,r/|c|)=[0,\,144/35)$, whose upper endpoint is approximately $4.11$. Then $
u^\star= rac{\lambda_ac+r}{s}=18/29-35\lambda_a/232\approx0.352$, and the exact optimizer is $x^\star= rac1{\lambda_a}(H^{-1}g-
u^\star H^{-1}b)= ig((2\sqrt{985}+5)/290,\,(65-3\sqrt{985})/580 ig)\approx(0.234,\,-0.050)$. Checks using this unrounded optimizer give $c+b^{	op}x^\star=0$ and $	frac12x^{\star	op}Hx^\star=0.050=\delta$ (both active), while $g^{	op}x^\star=(7\sqrt{985}+90)/1450\approx0.214$. The exact dual value is $D_a(\lambda_a)=\sqrt{(q-r^2/s)(2\delta-c^2/s)}- rac{rc}{s}=(7\sqrt{985}+90)/1450$: zero duality gap. For comparison, $D_b$ at its projected minimiser $\lambda_b=\max ig(\sqrt{q/(2\delta)},\,r/|c| ig)=\max ig(\sqrt{184/35},\,144/35 ig)=144/35\approx4.11$ is $ rac{q}{2\lambda_b}+\lambda_b\delta=23/360+36/175=3397/12600\approx0.270$, strictly greater than the exact $D_a(\lambda_a)$, which confirms $\lambda^\star=\lambda_a$ (the $\Lambda_a$ case of regime 2). Enter these values in the explorer (with $H_{12}=0.5$, $H_{22}=1$) to see the step.

u)$ for $\lambda\gt0$, $
u\ge0$, and show that $D$ is jointly convex. (b) Show that if the TRPO step satisfies the linearised constraint, $c+r\sqrt{2\delta/q}\le0$, then $(\lambda,

u D= rac{
u s-r}{\lambda}-c=- rac{\lambda_0c+r}{\lambda_0}\ge0$, the correct sign for a minimiser on the boundary $
